subject: Order Form SLA: scope of operational exceptions & credit calculations
messages:
From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@brightline.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form SLA - questions on maintenance exclusions and credit math

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal & SRE teams reviewed the draft order form and attached a redline (Brightline_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf). A few items we need clarified before procurement can move to signature:

- Maintenance windows: the draft allows 24x7 rolling maintenance with 8-hour notice for minor patches. Our SREs prefer defined monthly windows or blackout windows during product launches. Can Redwood commit to a maximum of 4 recurring maintenance hours per month (outside blackout windows) or provide an operational exception process?

- Emergency maintenance: need explicit language about advance notice where possible, and that emergency maintenance >2 hours triggers a follow-up RCA and a one-time SLA credit (not just a support ticket).

- Service credits: your order form caps credits at 10% of the monthly invoice. We asked legal to confirm the calculation — Brightline wants credit calculated proportionally per-minute of downtime beyond the uptime threshold rather than a flat slab.

- Uptime target: we understand you offer 99.9% for this tier. If we agree to a 99.95% target (we have compliance needs), what would the credit schedule look like?

Can you loop in ops/legal on your side and propose explicit language or an exception workflow? Ideally procurement would like a revised redline or a short playbook describing how exceptions (blackouts, launches) are handled operationally.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if easier.

Erin Walsh
Director, Procurement
Brightline Inc.
Attachment: Brightline_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@brightline.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form SLA - questions on maintenance exclusions and credit math

Erin —

Appreciate the clear ask and the redline. Looping in Lauren (legal) and Jordan (Customer Ops) so we can give a single response and proposed language. Quick summary from Redwood's side before Lauren weighs in formally:

- Maintenance windows: we can commit to a default of 4 hours/month scheduled maintenance (two 2-hour windows) with the option for customers to define blackout windows for launches with 14-day advance notice. For critical security patches we reserve the right to perform emergency maintenance with as-much-notice-as-possible; we agree to post an RCA if emergency maintenance exceeds 60 minutes of downtime.

- Emergency maintenance credits: we are open to an automatic credit trigger for emergency maintenance that causes an availability interruption >2 hours. We'd want to limit credits for emergency maintenance to a single incident per quarter for material upgrades to avoid abuse.

- Credit calculation: we prefer a proportional per-minute calculation tied to the monthly invoice (your suggestion). Typical formula we use: credit = (minutes_outage / minutes_in_month) * monthly_fee * credit_multiplier. We suggest a multiplier cap of 1.0 for standard outages and up to 1.5 for P1 incidents caused by Redwood platform defects.

- Uptime 99.95% ask: moving to 99.95% for this tier would require a commitment on both sides: reserved capacity and proactive batching/replicas for your production region. We can propose a 99.95 target with a steeper credit curve — e.g., credits begin at 99.95 and scale faster than at 99.9. I'll let Lauren draft precise language.

I've attached our counter redline (Redwood_SLA_Counter_20280618.docx) with tracked changes for the maintenance and credits sections. Next steps: Lauren, can you prepare suggested clauses (we should include an operational exception flow + an incident classification table)? Jordan — any operational constraints we should call out (maintenance lead time, blackout handling, surge capacity for launches)?

Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Counter_20280618.docx
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@brightline.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form SLA - questions on maintenance exclusions and credit math

Hi Erin, Kimberly, Jordan —

Thanks — I reviewed both redlines and propose the following (high-level) edits to be inserted in the MSA/order form:

1) Scheduled Maintenance (new subsection):
- Scheduled maintenance events are limited to a cumulative 4 hours per calendar month by default. Customer may designate up to two blackout windows per quarter (maximum 72 hours each) with at least 14 days' notice.
- For platform upgrades that require wider windows, Redwood will submit an Operational Exception Request that includes scope, rollback plan, and risk assessment. Customer approval is required for exceptions that exceed 8 hours in a single event.

2) Emergency Maintenance and RCA:
- Emergency maintenance that is reasonably unforeseeable and required to prevent material customer impact is permitted, but Redwood will provide best-effort notice and a post-event RCA for any emergency maintenance that results in an availability impact exceeding 60 minutes.

3) Availability & Credit Calculation: replace existing slab with per-minute proportional credits. Proposed formula (to insert):
- credit = (downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_billing_period) * monthly_fee * multiplier; where multiplier = 1.0 for standard availability breaches; multiplier = 1.5 for breaches attributable to Redwood platform defects as determined by mutually agreed incident classification.
- Credit cap: credits for availability breaches shall not exceed 30% of the monthly invoice for any single billing period.

4) 99.95% option language (optional rider):
- If Customer opts into a 99.95% availability tier, Redwood will operate dedicated capacity for the Customer's production region. Credits for this tier start at 99.95% and use the same per-minute formula with a lower threshold for credit (i.e., credits begin at a smaller deviation) and a higher maximum cap of 40% for the billing period. Such a rider requires a 60-day implementation lead time and a usage commitment (to be defined in the order form).

5) Escalation and Dispute Process:
- Add an SLA dispute matrix: initial assessment (Redwood) within 5 business days, joint review within 10 business days, binding arbitration trigger only after 30 days if unresolved.

Jordan — a couple of operational asks for you: can you confirm the implementation lead times for a 99.95 rider and whether we can offer a 60-day window reliably? Also confirm how we calculate "downtime_minutes" when partial-region impact happens (we should use affected-region weighted minutes).

Erin — if this aligns with Brightline's expectations I can convert the above into tracked-change text and push a revised PDF by EOD. If you want the 99.95 rider, flag separately and we'll include the usage commit language.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@brightline.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, procurement@brightline.com
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form SLA - questions on maintenance exclusions and credit math

Lauren / Kimberly —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed proposal. Brightline is generally comfortable with the approach and the per-minute proportional calculation — that addresses our main concern. A few follow-ups:

- Credit cap: Brightline would prefer a 35% single-period cap for the 99.95 rider (we're willing to accept 30% for the standard 99.9 tier). Is Redwood comfortable with 35% as the upper bound for the premium tier?

- Emergency maintenance frequency: your limitation of one creditable emergency maintenance incident per quarter is acceptable so long as Redwood commits to a documented post-incident remediation plan and priority engineering resources for follow-up.

- Blackout windows: procurement will mark two blackout windows for our Q4 launch (dates to be confirmed). We will use the Operational Exception Request for any exception >8 hours.

Next steps: please send the tracked-change redline reflecting the bullet points in Lauren's note. Once we have that PDF I'll route to our legal/procurement and aim to sign the order form pending the small cap change on the premium rider. We can do a quick call if helpful — available Thu or Fri morning PT.

Erin Walsh
Director, Procurement
Brightline Inc.
